review: Text reviewed for success rolls, equipment and difficulty modifiers, timing, long projects, outcome purchases and contests. Existing shared arithmetic requires explicit regression mappings; timing entries remain partial. No complete expanded dispatch is claimed.

entries.acceptance: Resolve three dice against the effective target, with success at or below it; apply modifiers to the target rather than the dice total.
A permitted roll of three or four succeeds and seventeen or eighteen fails regardless of the target; distinguish this from whether the attempt is permitted at all.
Reject ordinary success-roll attempts below effective target three before consuming randomness; preserve the explicit active-defense exception.
Combine applicable modifiers unless a rule declares replacement or exclusion; retain base and effective scores separately in structured outcomes.
Choose the best eligible default, cap the underlying attribute at twenty for attribute defaults only, and reject untrained actions without a default.
Expose signed target-minus-roll margin and the corresponding success/failure magnitude for downstream effects; extreme outcomes still preserve their rolled values.
A failed attempt that kills the actor or destroys its target cannot be retried as though the original task remains available.
Apply failed-attempt damage and the required elapsed interval before another permitted attempt; persistent consequences survive retries.
For repeatable harmless failures, apply -1 on the second attempt, -2 on the third and so on until success or abandonment; bind this history to the same task rather than a parser surface.
Ordinarily repeated actions such as attacks and long-task contributions retry with their usual time and without the generic escalating retry penalty.

In an ordinary quick contest a success beats a failure; among two successes greater success margin wins, and among two failures smaller failure margin wins. Equal margins with equal success status tie.
Compute victory margin from the two signed margins for all success/failure combinations, and report ties without inventing a winner.
For resistance contests, an attacking failure loses immediately without rolling resistance; preserve this random-consumption difference from ordinary quick contests.
Only a successful attacker that also wins the contest affects the subject; ties always protect the resisting subject.
In a regular contest only one success against the other failure ends the contest; both-success and both-failure rounds continue, with one declared time interval consumed per round.
If both scores are six or less, raise the lower to ten and add the same amount to the higher; five versus three becomes twelve versus ten.

If both scores are at least fourteen but the over-twenty ratio rule does not apply, lower the smaller score to ten and subtract the same amount from the larger; nineteen versus sixteen becomes thirteen versus ten.
If both scores exceed twenty, set the smaller to ten and multiply the larger by ten divided by the original smaller, rounding down; six hundred versus five hundred becomes twelve versus ten.

For a supernatural attack resisted by a living or sapient subject, cap attacker effective skill at the higher of sixteen and actual defender resistance; do not raise an attacker already below that cap.
An authored task assessment identifies meaningful risk or gain and whether a roll is needed; trivial actions and ordinary daily work normally do not roll, while monthly job checks remain separate.

An information task declares hidden resolution, world facts and success/failure disclosures; player-visible results must not leak the roll, concealed opposition or whether supplied information is false.
Secretly assess relevant senses and danger warnings without revealing that a concealed threat exists merely by requesting a public roll.
The author selects a task-wide difficulty independently of actor-specific modifiers and records any aggregate replacement, preventing the same circumstance from being penalized twice.

Outside attacks, critical consequences use a specific authored outcome for the task, with favorable success and adverse failure effects; attacks instead route through their applicable critical tables.

Declare whether the task permits retries, when its outcome becomes knowable, and its retry interval, damage and abandonment conditions; preserve that policy across parser, structured and dialogue actions.
Declare the contest round duration from its activity; combat rounds take one second while noncombat contests may consume much longer intervals.
Rolls three and four are critical successes for a permitted roll.
Roll five is critical success at effective target fifteen or more.
Roll six is critical success at effective target sixteen or more.
Roll eighteen is always critical failure.
Roll seventeen is critical failure at effective target fifteen or less and ordinary failure at sixteen or more.
Failure by at least ten is critical failure; test the nine-versus-ten margin boundary.
The automatic difficulty band permits a modifier from 10 through 10; author choice remains distinct from equipment, language and other personal modifiers.
The trivial difficulty band permits a modifier from 8 through 9; author choice remains distinct from equipment, language and other personal modifiers.
The very-easy difficulty band permits a modifier from 6 through 7; author choice remains distinct from equipment, language and other personal modifiers.
The easy difficulty band permits a modifier from 4 through 5; author choice remains distinct from equipment, language and other personal modifiers.
The very-favorable difficulty band permits a modifier from 2 through 3; author choice remains distinct from equipment, language and other personal modifiers.
The favorable difficulty band permits a modifier from 1 through 1; author choice remains distinct from equipment, language and other personal modifiers.
The average difficulty band permits a modifier from 0 through 0; author choice remains distinct from equipment, language and other personal modifiers.
The unfavorable difficulty band permits a modifier from -1 through -1; author choice remains distinct from equipment, language and other personal modifiers.
The very-unfavorable difficulty band permits a modifier from -3 through -2; author choice remains distinct from equipment, language and other personal modifiers.
The hard difficulty band permits a modifier from -5 through -4; author choice remains distinct from equipment, language and other personal modifiers.

The dangerous difficulty band permits a modifier from -9 through -8; author choice remains distinct from equipment, language and other personal modifiers.
The extreme difficulty band permits a modifier from -10 through -10; author choice remains distinct from equipment, language and other personal modifiers.
Apply equipment modifier -10. No equipment for a technological skill, if the task is possible at all.
Apply equipment modifier -5. No equipment for a nontechnological skill, if use is possible.
Apply equipment modifier -5. Improvised equipment for a technological skill.
Apply equipment modifier -2. Improvised equipment for a nontechnological skill.
Apply equipment modifier 0. Appropriate basic equipment.
Apply equipment modifier 1. Good equipment, priced at approximately five times basic cost.
Apply equipment modifier 2. Fine equipment, priced at approximately twenty times basic cost.
Best available equipment at a technology level gives floor(technology/2), with minimum +2; it is not automatically available for purchase.
For basic or better equipment, apply -1 per important missing item in addition to quality.
For basic or better equipment, apply an authored -1 through -3 damage modifier in addition to quality; bind the condition to the actual equipment used.
For an eligible noncombat task, taking 2 times its ordinary duration grants +1; commit the resulting elapsed time only once.
For an eligible noncombat task, taking 4 times its ordinary duration grants +2; commit the resulting elapsed time only once.
For an eligible noncombat task, taking 8 times its ordinary duration grants +3; commit the resulting elapsed time only once.
For an eligible noncombat task, taking 15 times its ordinary duration grants +4; commit the resulting elapsed time only once.
For an eligible noncombat task, taking 30 times its ordinary duration grants +5; commit the resulting elapsed time only once.
Taking 90% of ordinary duration imposes -1; reject when natural laws, equipment limits or skill-specific timing prohibit this reduction.
Taking 80% of ordinary duration imposes -2; reject when natural laws, equipment limits or skill-specific timing prohibit this reduction.
Taking 70% of ordinary duration imposes -3; reject when natural laws, equipment limits or skill-specific timing prohibit this reduction.
Taking 60% of ordinary duration imposes -4; reject when natural laws, equipment limits or skill-specific timing prohibit this reduction.
Taking 50% of ordinary duration imposes -5; reject when natural laws, equipment limits or skill-specific timing prohibit this reduction.
Taking 40% of ordinary duration imposes -6; reject when natural laws, equipment limits or skill-specific timing prohibit this reduction.
Taking 30% of ordinary duration imposes -7; reject when natural laws, equipment limits or skill-specific timing prohibit this reduction.
Taking 20% of ordinary duration imposes -8; reject when natural laws, equipment limits or skill-specific timing prohibit this reduction.
Taking 10% of ordinary duration imposes -9; reject when natural laws, equipment limits or skill-specific timing prohibit this reduction.
The cinematic option permits one instant attempt at -10, with no repeat loophole through new contexts or command surfaces; it is disabled unless chosen for the campaign.
Skill-specific timing, including spell rituals and ceremonial casting, overrides the generic haste and extra-time table.

The author names the task, its normal duration, whether additional deliberation can help and whether rushing is physically possible; an unconstrained boolean is not the finished adjudication contract.
A long project declares required person-hours by labor type and eligible contributing skills; each owned contribution records worker, interval, labor type and result.
The normal daily labor allowance is eight hours per worker; at shift end each worker rolls the skill used, with hidden rolls for nonplayer workers where appropriate.
Ordinary success credits the hours worked, critical success credits 150%, ordinary failure credits half, and critical failure credits none and destroys 2d previously completed person-hours.
A supervisor must work the full shift coordinating rather than also contributing ordinary labor; the author selects administration for organization or leadership for inspiration.
A successful supervisor grants +1 to the workers' daily rolls, critical success grants +2, and any failure contributes no benefit.
A nonplayer worker requires the applicable influence result to work an extended shift; do not bypass that social procedure with project permission.
Any day over eight hours requires a health check; apply -1 per hour over ten and no duration penalty for the interval over eight through ten.
After a failed endurance check, penalize the work roll by the larger of two or the failure magnitude and spend that many fatigue points; a successful work roll can still credit the longer shift.
Critical endurance failure additionally prevents work the next day; keep this restriction across save and undo.
Changing required hours through haste or extra time applies its corresponding modifier to every worker in that labor category, without also crediting unworked hours.
Outcome purchases are an explicit campaign option with any per-session spending limit; they draw from the existing bonus-point bank.
Only the actor's most recent eligible success roll can be altered; bind purchase to that outcome identity and apply dependent consequences consistently rather than rerolling.
Upgrading critical failure to ordinary failure costs two bonus points.
Upgrading ordinary failure to success costs one bonus point.
Upgrading ordinary success to critical success costs two points, subject to the campaign restriction on purchased critical successes, including combat.
Add transition costs for multiple shifts; critical failure to critical success costs five points, paid once for the committed change.
Adding an accepted plausible scene element after ordinary success or a no-roll situation costs two points; after critical success it costs one and replaces other beneficial critical effects.

An authored proposal must be plausible, acceptable to the participating players and consistent with established facts; accepted scene additions become persistent world facts and rejected proposals consume no points.

exclusions.reason: Exclude source wording, named illustrative characters and narrative anecdotes. Preserve numeric examples and specific adjudication decisions as neutral obligations.
